desc: Parse input, build adjacency list with edge indices.
Split edge list into left half (size L) and right half (size R).
For each subset of left half (0..2^L-1): count selected edges, run 0-1 BFS from 1 to N using edge weights (0 if not selected, 1 if selected), record distance.
For each subset of right half: similarly compute distance and store in a map keyed by selected count -> max distance.
Combine: for each left subset distance dL with c selected, look up max dR for count K-c; track global maximum of dL + dR.
Discard the meet-in-the-middle approach as infeasible for M=100.
Implement a flow-based feasibility check: for a given L, construct a network where we want to ensure at least L selected edges on every path.
Use binary search on L from 0 to N-1, and compute the maximum feasible L.
Test the flow-based solution on the sample inputs to verify correctness.
